name: Cabergoline
route_note: oral tablet once or twice weekly for hyperprolactinaemia; single dose for lactation inhibition

discovery.note: An ergoline derivative with a very long half-life.

tagline: A twice-weekly dopamine agonist that shrinks prolactin-secreting tumours
summary: Cabergoline is a long-acting ergot-derived dopamine agonist and the preferred treatment for hyperprolactinaemia and prolactinomas. Its use in Parkinson's disease has largely ended because high doses were linked to fibrotic heart-valve disease.
mechanism: Pituitary lactotroph cells are tonically inhibited by hypothalamic dopamine acting on D2 receptors. Cabergoline is a potent, long-acting D2 agonist that suppresses prolactin synthesis and secretion and shrinks most prolactinomas.

Its agonism at serotonin 5-HT2B receptors on heart valve interstitial cells can stimulate fibroblast proliferation, the proposed mechanism of valvulopathy at the high doses once used in Parkinson's disease.
uses: Hyperprolactinaemic disorders, idiopathic or due to pituitary adenoma
Inhibition or suppression of lactation (EU and other regions)
Acromegaly and other pituitary tumours (off-label adjunct)

history.title: Cabergoline vs bromocriptine
history.detail: A multicentre trial shows cabergoline more effective and better tolerated than bromocriptine for hyperprolactinaemic amenorrhoea (NEJM 1994).

history.title: US approval
history.detail: FDA approves Dostinex for hyperprolactinaemia in December 1996.

history.title: Valvulopathy studies
history.detail: Two NEJM studies link cabergoline and pergolide in Parkinson's disease to cardiac valve regurgitation.

history.title: EU restrictions
history.detail: The EMA restricts ergot-derived dopamine agonists in Parkinson's disease, requiring echocardiographic monitoring and lowering maximum dose.

history.title: Endocrine Society guideline
history.detail: The Endocrine Society recommends cabergoline as the preferred dopamine agonist for hyperprolactinaemia and prolactinomas.

facts: Its 63–69 hour half-life allows dosing once or twice a week.
Cabergoline normalises prolactin in most patients with microprolactinomas.

references.title: Schade R et al. Dopamine agonists and the risk of cardiac-valve regurgitation (NEJM 2007)
